speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg in detail, including when it started and any changes you've noticed. Additionally, do you have any history of trauma, insect bites, or recent travel to tropical regions?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous leishmaniasis (likely secondary to ant bite inoculation, exacerbated by immunosuppression from prior corticosteroid use and Crohn's disease).

REQUEST TEST: Leishmaniasis Serology
REQUEST TEST: Skin Biopsy with Histopathology
REQUEST IMAGES: Lesion photograph showing ulceration and border characteristics.
